chapter: Wartime South and the Ernie Fields band
title: Leading a band in Alexandria, Louisiana
summary: After the funeral he joins a group playing Alexandria near Camp Polk, is voted leader, and meets Lips Rose again.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So anyway, I got back to gigging around Detroit. And before long, my grandmother passed, and I went back to the funeral. And while I was there, some friends of mine that I had played with, one in particular that I didn't mention, who had played with the Doc Palmer Orchestra, the first orchestra I played with, Jack Scott, the guitarist... And there was an alto saxophone player with Don Dunbar's orchestra, Bolden(?) Townsend, and his wife, Micki Gwynn(?), who had also played the piano and sang with the Don Dunbar Orchestra. They put a group together to go down to Alexandria, Louisiana, to play at a nightclub. There was a hotel with the nightclub downstairs, and we lived upstairs; it was called the Graystone Ballroom. We had a nice little group together. We had a little bass player from home named
Rush(?); I don't remember his last name.

And while we were working this particular job... It was during the War. There was plenty of soldiers, we were near Camp Polk and everything was happening. And it gave me an opportunity to see Lips(?) Rose again, the great saxophone player, and his wife Edith Kirk(?), because they were stationed in Alexandria. So that was nice, to be around them again.
